title: CES 2027: Crosshub's V·Pay Verifies Who Is Speaking and What Was Approved Within 1.2 Seconds - 에이빙

CES 2027: Crosshub's V·Pay Verifies Who Is Speaking and What Was Approved Within 1.2 Seconds | 
 CES 2027: Crosshub's V·Pay Verifies Who Is Speaking and What Was Approved Within 1.2 Seconds
 - CES 2027 Innovation Awards FinTech Honoree ties a one-time spoken phrase to a registered device, a voiceprint and the exact transaction
 2026-11-16     Davis K. Reporter 
 Photo - CES 2027 
 Paying without a screen or keypad is becoming common, in a car, through glasses or at a drive-through. Approving the payment safely in those moments is the harder part.
 Crosshub Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in FinTech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for V·Pay, a voiceprint-verified payment solution.
 V·Pay lets users approve a specific payment with one verified, transaction-bound phrase. Passkeys confirm account access and voice assistants interpret commands, while V·Pay verifies who is speaking, which registered device is in use, and whether the phrase matches the exact merchant, amount and a one-time nonce.
 Photo- CES 2027 
 The technology is a triple voice authorization method aimed at screenless and AI agent-driven payment environments. When a high-risk transaction occurs, such as a payment, high-value transfer, login or account recovery, it verifies the registered device, the speaker's voiceprint and a dynamic one-time authorization phrase at the same time, within 1.2 seconds. Rather than simply recognizing a voice command, it analyzes both the speech content (what was approved) and the frequency, intonation and pronunciation patterns (who approved it). Because the system generates a new phrase for every transaction, recordings, replay attacks and AI-generated voice cloning cannot pass verification.
 The voice AI folds speaker verification, anti-spoofing, phrase validation, device trust and transaction risk signals into a single authorization decision. Delivered through mobile SDKs and APIs, it links with existing wallets, payment gateways, merchant apps and AI agents without dedicated authentication hardware. Its risk-adaptive structure requests additional step-up authentication only when it detects anomalies. V·Pay is built for smart glasses, in-car payments, drive-throughs, wearables, kiosks and other settings where screens or manual input are impractical.
 Digital student ID ‘Smart ID’ by Crosshub | Photo - Crosshub 
 Crosshub won the Best of Innovation award in the FinTech category at CES 2026 with its Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI)-based identity authentication solution IDBlock and its payment API infrastructure B-Pay. V·Pay is finishing MVP development, and the company is preparing for commercialization through proof-of-concept (PoC) testing in the financial and payment sectors.
 Hae-in Jung, Head of North America at Crosshub, said voice assistants on mobile phones specialize in searches and device control, while V·Pay serves as a payment-dedicated authentication layer that verifies not only what was authorized but also who authorized it at the exact moment the payment is processed. She said the company will start with an additional authentication method for high-risk, high-value transactions and expand it into a core authorization tool for screenless payments and AI agent commerce, such as drive-throughs, in-vehicle payments and smart glasses.
 Voice payment authentication ‘V·Pay’ by Crosshub | Photo - Crosshub 
 The CES Innovation Awards program, an annual competition honoring outstanding design and engineering in consumer technology products, recognizes all recipients as Honorees at two levels. The Honoree level covers products that score above the scoring threshold in each category, while Best of Innovation goes to the highest-scoring Honorees. A panel of industry expert judges and global media scores each product on engineering and functionality, aesthetic and design, and what makes it unique and innovative.
